text:
Let y = y(x) be the solution of the differential equation, 
$xy'- y = x^{2}($xcosx + sinx), x > 0. if y ($π$) = $π$ then 
$y^{''}\left (\frac{π}{2}\right )+y\left (\frac{π}{2}\right )$ is equal to :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 4th September Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$xy^{'}-y=x^{2}(x\mathrm{cosx}+sinx),x>0,y(π)=π$

$y^{'}-\frac{1}{x}y=x\{x\cos x+\sin x\}$

$I.F.=e^{-\int \frac{1}{2}dx}=e^{-\ln x}=\frac{1}{x}$

$\therefore$ $y.\frac{1}{x}=\int \frac{1}{x}.x(xcosx+sinx)dx$

$\frac{y}{x}$ = $\int (x\cos x+\sin x)dx$

$=x\sin x+C$

$\frac{y}{x}$ = $x\sin x+C$

$\Rightarrow y=x^{2}=\sin x+cx$

x = $π$, y = $π$

$π$ = $π$c $\Rightarrow$ C = 1

$y=x^{2}\sin x+x\Rightarrow y\left (\frac{π}{2}\right )=\frac{π^{2}}{4}+\frac{π}{2}$

$y^{'}=2x\sin x+x^{2}\cos x+1$

y" = $2\sin x+2x\cos x+2x\cos x-x^{2}\sin x$

y" $\left (\frac{π}{2}\right )=2-\frac{π^{2}}{4}$

$\Rightarrow y\left (\frac{π}{2}\right )$ + y" $\left (\frac{π}{2}\right )=2+\frac{π}{2}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2020 (Online) 4th September Morning Slot

text:
Let $\frac{x^{2}}{a^{2}}+\frac{y^{2}}{b^{2}}=1$ (a > b) be a given ellipse, length of whose latus rectum is 10. If its eccentricity is the maximum value of the function, 
$𝜙(t)=\frac{5}{12}+t-t^{2}$,  then $a^{2} + b^{2}$ is equal to :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 4th September Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Given ellipse $\frac{x^{2}}{a^{2}}+\frac{y^{2}}{b^{2}}=1$ (a > b)

Length of latus rectum $=\frac{2b^{2}}{a}=10$

$𝜙(t)=\frac{5}{12}+t-t^{2}$

$=\frac{8}{12}-\left (t-\frac{1}{2}\right )^{2}$

$\therefore$ $𝜙(t)_{\max }=\frac{8}{12}=\frac{2}{3}$

$\therefore$ eccentricity (e) = $\frac{2}{3}$

Also, $e^{2}=1-\frac{b^{2}}{a^{2}}$

$\Rightarrow \frac{4}{9}=1-\frac{b^{2}}{a^{2}}$

$\Rightarrow \frac{b^{2}}{a^{2}}=\frac{5}{9}$

$\Rightarrow \frac{b^{2}}{a}\times \frac{1}{a}=\frac{5}{9}$

$\Rightarrow \frac{5}{a}=\frac{5}{9}$

$\Rightarrow a=9$

$\therefore$ $b^{2}=5\times 9=45$

$\therefore$ $a^{2}+b^{2}=81+45=126$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2020 (Online) 4th September Morning Slot

text: Let $f(x)=\int \frac{\sqrt{x}}{(1+x)^{2}}dx(x\geq 0)$.  Then f(3) – f(1) is equal to :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 4th September Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\int \frac{\sqrt{x}}{(1+x)^{2}}dx(x>0)$

Put $x = \tan ^{2}θ$ $\Rightarrow$ dx = 2tan$θ\sec ^{2}θ$d$θ$

$I=\int \frac{2\tan ^{2}θ.\sec ^{2}θ}{\sec ^{4}θ}dθ=\int 2\sin ^{2}θdθ=\int (1-\cos 2θ)dθ$

$=θ-\frac{\sin 2θ}{2}+c$

$\Rightarrow f(x)=θ-\frac{1}{2}\times \frac{2\tan θ}{1+\tan ^{2}θ}+c$ $f(x)=θ-\frac{\tan θ}{1+\tan ^{2}θ}+c=\tan ^{-1}\sqrt{x}-\frac{\sqrt{x}}{1+x}+c$

Now $f(3)-f(1)=\tan ^{-1}\left (\sqrt{3}\right )-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{1+3}-\tan ^{-1}(1)+\frac{1}{2}$

$=\frac{π}{3}-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{4}-\frac{π}{4}+\frac{1}{2}$

$=\frac{π}{12}+\frac{1}{2}-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{4}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2020 (Online) 4th September Morning Slot

text: Let f be a twice differentiable function on (1, 6). If f(2) = 8, f’(2) = 5, f’(x) $\geq$ 1 and f''(x) $\geq$ 4, for all x $\in$ (1, 6), then :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 4th September Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Given, $f^{'}(x)\geq 1$

$\therefore$ $\int\limits _{2}^{5}f^{'}(x)dx\geq \int\limits _{2}^{5}dx$

$\Rightarrow f(5)-f(2)\geq 3$

$\Rightarrow f(5)-8\geq 3$

$\Rightarrow f(5)\geq 11$ ...(1)

Also, $f^{''}(x)\geq 4$

$\therefore$ $\int\limits _{2}^{5}f^{''}(x)dx\geq \int\limits _{2}^{5}4dx$

$\Rightarrow f^{'}(5)-f^{'}(2)\geq 4(3)$

$\Rightarrow f^{'}(5)-5\geq 12$

$\Rightarrow f^{'}(5)\geq 17$ ...(2)

From (1) and (2),

$f^{'}(5)+f^{'}(5)\geq 11+17$

$\Rightarrow f^{'}(5)+f^{'}(5)\geq 28$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2020 (Online) 4th September Morning Slot

text:
Let $α$ and $β$ be the roots of $x^{2} - 3x + p=0$ and $γ$ and $δ$ be the roots of $x^{2} - 6x + q = 0$. If $α,β,γ,δ$
form a geometric progression.Then ratio (2q + p) : (2q - p) is:
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 4th September Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$α$ and $β$ are the roots of $x^{2}$ $-$ 3x + p = 0

$\therefore$ $α$ + $β$ = 3 and $αβ$ = p

$γ$ and $δ$ are the roots of $x^{2}$ $-$ 6x + q = 0

$\therefore$ $γ$ + $δ$ = 6 and $γδ$ = q

Given that, $α$, $β$, $γ$, $δ$ are in G.P.

$\therefore$ Let $α$ = a, $β$ = ar, $γ$ $= ar^{2}$ and $δ$ $= ar^{3}$

As $α$ + $β$ = 3

$\Rightarrow$ a + ar = 3

$\Rightarrow$ a(1 + r) = 3 ...(1)

Also $γ$ + $δ$ = 6

$\Rightarrow$ $ar^{2} + ar^{3} = 6$

$\Rightarrow$ $ar^{2} (1 + r) = 6 ... (2)$

Dividing (2) by (1),

$r^{2} = 2$

$\Rightarrow r=\sqrt{2}$

$\therefore$ $a=\frac{3}{1+\sqrt{2}}$

So, $α=\frac{3}{1+\sqrt{2}}$, $β=\frac{3\sqrt{2}}{1+\sqrt{2}}$, $γ=\frac{3\times 2}{1+\sqrt{2}}$, $δ=\frac{3(2\sqrt{2)}}{1+\sqrt{2}}$

$\therefore$ $p=αβ=\frac{9\sqrt{2}}{\left (1+\sqrt{2}\right )^{2}}$

and $q=γδ=\frac{36\sqrt{2}}{\left (1+\sqrt{2}\right )^{2}}$

Now, $\frac{2q+p}{2q-p}$

$=\frac{\frac{72\sqrt{2}}{\left (1+\sqrt{2}\right )2}+\frac{9\sqrt{2}}{\left (1+\sqrt{2}\right )2}}{\frac{72\sqrt{2}}{\left (1+\sqrt{2}\right )2}-\frac{9\sqrt{2}}{\left (1+\sqrt{2}\right )2}}$

$=\frac{72\sqrt{2}+9\sqrt{2}}{72\sqrt{2}-9\sqrt{2}}$

$=\frac{81}{63}$

$=\frac{9}{7}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2020 (Online) 4th September Morning Slot

text:
Let $u=\frac{2z+i}{z-ki}$, z = x + iy and k > 0.  If the curve represented
 by Re(u) + Im(u) = 1 intersects the y-axis at the points P and Q where PQ = 5, then the value of k is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 4th September Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Given, z = x + iy

and $u=\frac{2z+i}{z-ki}$

$=\frac{2(x+iy)+i}{(x+iy)-ki}$

$=\frac{2x+i(2y+1)}{x+i(y-k)}\times \frac{x-i(y-k)}{x-i(y-k)}$

$=\frac{2x^{2}+(2y+1)(y-k)+i(2xy+x-2xy+2kx)}{x^{2}+(y-k)^{2}}$

Given, 

$\mathrm{Re}(u)+\mathrm{Im}(u)=1$

$\Rightarrow \frac{2x^{2}+(2y+1)(y-k)}{x^{2}+(y-k)^{2}}+\frac{x+2kx}{x^{2}+(y-k)^{2}}=1$

$\Rightarrow 2x^{2}+(2y+1)(y-k)+x+2kx=x^{2}+(y-k)^{2}$

This curve intersect the y-axis at point P and Q, so at point P and Q x = 0

Putting x = 0 at the above equation,

$\therefore$ $(2y+1)(y-k)=(y-k)^{2}$

$\Rightarrow 2y^{2}+y-2yk-k=y^{2}+k^{2}-2ky$

$\Rightarrow y^{2}+y-(k+k^{2})=0$

Let roots of this quadratic equation $y_{1}$ and $y_{2}$

$\therefore$ Point $P (0, y_{1})$ and $Q (0, y_{2})$

and $y_{{}_{1}}+y_{2}=1$ , $y_{1}y_{2}=-k-k^{2}$

$\therefore$ $(y_{1}-y_{2})^{2}=(y_{1}+y_{2})^{2}-4y_{1}y_{2}$

$=1+4k+4k^{2}$

$\Rightarrow |y_{1}-y_{2}|=\sqrt{1+4k+4k^{2}}$

Given, PQ = 5

$\Rightarrow |y_{1}-y_{2}|=5$

$\Rightarrow \sqrt{1+4k+4k^{2}}=5$

$\Rightarrow k^{2}+k-6=0$

$\Rightarrow k=-3,2$

So, k = 2 (Given k > 0)
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2020 (Online) 4th September Morning Slot

text:
If $A=\left [\begin{array}{ll} \cos θ & i\sin θ \\ i\sin θ & \cos θ \end{array}\right ]$, $\left (θ=\frac{π}{24}\right )$

and $A^{5}=\left [\begin{array}{ll} a & b \\ c & d \end{array}\right ]$, where $i=\sqrt{-1}$  then which one of the following is
not true?
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 4th September Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\because$ $A=\left [\begin{array}{ll} \cos θ & i\sin θ \\ i\sin θ & \cos θ \end{array}\right ]$

$\therefore$ $A^{n}=\left [\begin{array}{ll} \cos nθ & i\sin nθ \\ i\sin nθ & \cos nθ \end{array}\right ],n\in N$

$\thereforeA^{5}=\left [\begin{array}{ll} \cos 5θ & i\sin 5θ \\ i\sin 5θ & \cos 5θ \end{array}\right ]=\left [\begin{array}{ll} a & b \\ c & d \end{array}\right ]$

$\therefore$ $a=\cos 5θ,b=i\sin 5θ=c,d=\cos 5θ$

$\therefore$ $a^{2}-b^{2}=\cos ^{2}5θ+\sin ^{2}5θ=1$

$a^{2}-c^{2}=\cos ^{2}5θ+\sin ^{2}5θ=1$

$a^{2}-d^{2}=\cos ^{2}5θ-\cos ^{2}5θ=0$

$a^{2}+b^{2}=\cos ^{2}5θ-\sin ^{2}5θ=\cos 10θ=\cos \frac{10π}{24}$

and $0<\cos \frac{5π}{12}<1$

$\Rightarrow 0\leq a^{2}+b^{2}\leq 1$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2020 (Online) 4th September Morning Slot

text:
The mean and variance of 8 observations are 10 and 13.5, respectively. If 6 of these observations
are 5, 7, 10, 12, 14, 15, then the absolute difference of the remaining two observations is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 4th September Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Let the two remaining observations be x and y.

$\because$ $\bar{x}=10=\frac{5+7+10+12+14+15+x+y}{8}$

$\Rightarrow x+y=17$ ....(1)

$\because$ $\mathrm{var}(x)=13.5=\frac{25+49+100+144+196+225+x^{2}+y^{2}}{8}-(10)^{2}$

$\Rightarrow x^{2}+y^{2}=169$ ....(2)

From (1) and (2)

(x, y) = (12, 5) or (5, 12)

So $|x-y|=7$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2020 (Online) 4th September Morning Slot

text:
A survey shows that 63% of the people in a city read newspaper A whereas 76% read
newspaper B. If x% of the people read both the newspapers, then a possible value of x can be:
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 4th September Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
[IMG]


A $\cup$ B = 63 - x + x + 76 - x = 139 - x

As 139 - x $\leq$ 100

$\Rightarrow$ x $\geq$ 39

From Venn diagram, you can see x should be less than 76 and 63 otherwise only A newspaper or only B newspaper reader will be negative number.

Intersection of x $\leq$ 63 and x $\leq$76 is = x $\leq$ 63.

$\therefore$ 39 $\leq$ x $\leq$ 63

From options possible value of x = 55.

text:
If $\left (a+\sqrt{2}b\cos x\right )\left (a-\sqrt{2}b\cos y\right )=a^{2}-b^{2}$

 where a > b > 0, then $\frac{dx}{dy}at\left (\frac{π}{4},\frac{π}{4}\right )$ is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 4th September Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$(a+\sqrt{2}b\cos x)(a-\sqrt{2}b\cos y)=a^{2}-b^{2}$

$\Rightarrow a^{2}-\sqrt{2}ab\cos y+\sqrt{2}ab\cos x-2b^{2}\cos x\cos y=a^{2}-b^{2}$

Differentiating both sides :

$0-\sqrt{2}ab\left (-\sin y\frac{dy}{dx}\right )+\sqrt{2}ab(-\sin x)$

$-2b^{2}\left [\cos x\left (-\sin y\frac{dy}{dx}\right )+\cos y(-\sin x)\right ]=0$

At $\left (\frac{π}{4},\frac{π}{4}\right )$ :

$ab\frac{dy}{dx}-ab-2b^{2}\left (-\frac{1}{2}\frac{dy}{dx}-\frac{1}{2}\right )=0$

$\Rightarrow \frac{dx}{dy}=\frac{ab+b^{2}}{ab-b^{2}}=\frac{a+b}{a-b}$; a, b > 0
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2020 (Online) 4th September Morning Slot

text:
Suppose a differentiable function f(x) satisfies the identity 
$f(x+y) = f(x) + f(y) + xy^{2} + x^{2}y$, for all real x and y.

$\lim _{x\to 0}\frac{f(x)}{x}=1$,  then f'(3) is equal to $______$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 4th September Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Given, $f(x + y) = f(x) + f(y) + xy^{2} + x^{2}y ...(1)$

differentiating partially with respect to x,

$f'(x+y) = f'(x) + 0 + y^{2} + y(2x)$ [y = constant]

Put x = 0 and y = x

$\therefore$ $f'(x) = f'(0) + x^{2} ....(2)$

putting x = y = 0 at equation (1),

f(0) = 2f(0)

$\Rightarrow$ f(0) = 0

Given, $\lim _{x\to 0}\frac{f(x)}{x}=1$

This is in $\frac{0}{0}$ form, so we can apply L' hospital rule.

$\lim _{x\to 0}\frac{f^{'}(x)}{1}=1$

$\Rightarrow f^{'}(0)=1$

Putting value of f'(0) at equation (2), we get

$f'(x) = 1 + x^{2}$

$\therefore$ $f'(3) = 1 + 3^{2} = 10$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2020 (Online) 4th September Morning Slot

text:
The probability of a man hitting a target is $\frac{1}{10}$. The least number of shots required, so that the
probability of his hitting the target at least once is greater than $\frac{1}{4}$, is $____________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 4th September Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
We have, $1-$(probability of all shots results in failure out of n trials) > $\frac{1}{4}$

$\Rightarrow 1-\left (\frac{9}{10}\right )^{n}>\frac{1}{4}$

$\Rightarrow \frac{3}{4}>\left (\frac{9}{10}\right )^{n}\Rightarrow n\geq 3$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2020 (Online) 4th September Morning Slot
